122	// or math.MaxInt64 if no open appenders.
123	func (i *isolation) lowestAppendTime() int64 {
124		var lowest int64 = math.MaxInt64
125		i.appendMtx.RLock()
126		defer i.appendMtx.RUnlock()
127	
128		for a := i.appendsOpenList.next; a != i.appendsOpenList; a = a.next {

131			}
132		}

136	// State returns an object used to control isolation
137	// between a query and appends. Must be closed when complete.
138	func (i *isolation) State(mint, maxt int64) *isolationState {
139		i.appendMtx.RLock() // Take append mutex before read mutex.
140		defer i.appendMtx.RUnlock()
141	
142		// We need to track reads even when isolation is disabled, so that head
143		// truncation can wait till reads overlapping that range have finished.
144		isoState := &isolationState{
145			maxAppendID:       i.appendsOpenList.appendID,
146			lowWatermark:      i.appendsOpenList.next.appendID, // Lowest appendID from appenders, or lastAppendId.
147			incompleteAppends: make(map[uint64]struct{}, len(i.appendsOpen)),
148			isolation:         i,
149			mint:              mint,
150			maxt:              maxt,
151		}
152		for k := range i.appendsOpen {
153			isoState.incompleteAppends[k] = struct{}{}
154		}
155	
156		i.readMtx.Lock()
157		defer i.readMtx.Unlock()
158		isoState.prev = i.readsOpen
159		isoState.next = i.readsOpen.next
160		i.readsOpen.next.prev = isoState
161		i.readsOpen.next = isoState
162	
163		return isoState
164	}

166	// TraverseOpenReads iterates through the open reads and runs the given
167	// function on those states. The given function MUST NOT mutate the isolationState.
168	// The iteration is stopped when the function returns false or once all reads have been iterated.
169	func (i *isolation) TraverseOpenReads(f func(s *isolationState) bool) {
170		i.readMtx.RLock()
171		defer i.readMtx.RUnlock()
172		s := i.readsOpen.next
173		for s != i.readsOpen {
174			if !f(s) {
175				return
176			}
177			s = s.next
178		}
179	}

181	// newAppendID increments the transaction counter and returns a new transaction
182	// ID. The first ID returned is 1.
183	// Also returns the low watermark, to keep lock/unlock operations down.
184	func (i *isolation) newAppendID(minTime int64) (uint64, uint64) {
185		if i.disabled {
186			return 0, 0
187		}
188	
189		i.appendMtx.Lock()
190		defer i.appendMtx.Unlock()
191	
192		// Last used appendID is stored in head element.
193		i.appendsOpenList.appendID++
194	
195		app := i.appendersPool.Get().(*isolationAppender)
196		app.appendID = i.appendsOpenList.appendID
197		app.minTime = minTime
198		app.prev = i.appendsOpenList.prev
199		app.next = i.appendsOpenList
200	
201		i.appendsOpenList.prev.next = app
202		i.appendsOpenList.prev = app
203	
204		i.appendsOpen[app.appendID] = app
205		return app.appendID, i.lowWatermarkLocked()
206	}

units.headline: Adds package-level test hook invoked before head-view eviction
units.summary: New package-level func var that compactHeadViewLocked calls once and then resets to nil. It is nil in production, so the only runtime cost is a nil check. Only tests set it.
units.reason: Test-only hook, nil in production; only adds a nil check on the compaction path.

units.headline: Introduces headViewFactory func type for restricted head views
units.summary: Unexported func type used to parameterize compactHeadViewLocked. Declaring a type has no runtime effect by itself; the behavior lives in its callers.
units.reason: Unexported type declaration; behavior lives in compactHeadViewLocked and its callers.

units.headline: Introduces headSeriesEvictor func type with append-ID watermark contract
units.summary: Unexported func type plus doc comment describing the eviction contract. The claim that the watermark is always 0 with isolation disabled holds: lastAppendID returns 0 when isolation is disabled.
units.reason: Type declaration and documentation only; contract enforcement is in other units.

units.headline: Shared head-view compaction loop now captures an append-ID eviction watermark
units.summary: Pulls the per-chunk-range block write and reload loop into one shared helper. It also records lastAppendID before writing, skips the reload when the view is empty, and passes maxt and the watermark to the evictor. Eviction decides whether series data is dropped from the head, so a wrong decision loses data.

issues.title: Watermark misses appends opened before capture but committed later
issues.failure_scenario: An appender is created before compaction starts and gets appendID N; the watermark is also N. It commits a sample with ts <= head MaxTime after the block writer's isolation snapshot, which treats N as incomplete. The block leaves the sample out, hasAppendIDAbove(s, N) returns false, and the series is evicted. The sample is gone from the head, and on WAL replay the walExpiry for the evicted ref drops it too.

units.reason: Changes data-eviction safety logic and the persistence flow for head compaction.
focus: Whether the watermark should be the low watermark (oldest open append) rather than lastAppendID, so in-flight appenders are covered
Comment's 'guaranteed to contain all samples with appendID <= watermark' versus isolation's incompleteAppends behavior
Reload failure on a later chunk-range iteration leaves earlier blocks loaded while the series stay in the head

units.headline: CompactStaleHead delegates to the shared helper with an append-ID guard
units.summary: CompactStaleHead now uses compactHeadViewLocked with SelectedSeriesHead and truncateStaleSeries. Eviction now also requires that the series has no OOO data and no samples with appendID above the watermark, and the per-block log text changed.
units.reason: Changes the eviction predicate and code path of an existing production compaction.
focus: SelectedSeriesHead.NumSeries now uses the ref list length instead of NumStaleSeries; check this is equivalent for stale compaction
The extra watermark/OOO predicate may keep stale series in the head that were evicted before

units.headline: Test comment renames gcStaleSeries to gcSeries
units.summary: Only a comment in a test changes, to match the renamed function. No code or assertion is touched.
units.reason: Comment-only edit in a test file; no code changes.

units.headline: New test: late append before eviction survives restart
units.summary: Uses the hook to commit a sample between the block write and eviction, then checks the sample survives with isolation enabled. With isolation disabled the test expects the late sample to be lost, so that data loss is pinned as accepted behavior. It covers only appenders opened after the watermark, not in-flight ones.
units.reason: New test only; cannot change production behavior.
